title: Liverpool Player Ratings vs. Brentford: Moment of Madness Breaks 238-Day Streak
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom12:23 PM EDTAlexander Isak scored the decisive goal. / Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesLONDON — Liverpool had Alexander Isak, Víctor Muñoz and, most of all, Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk to thank for a 2–1 win at the Gtech Community Stadium on Saturday.

Andoni Iraola’s visitors were deservedly trailing 1–0 before Yarmoliuk became enveloped in a cloud of red mist on the cusp of halftime, delivering the gentlest of headbutts that would have a far more profound impact on the contest than its intended recipient, Jérémy Jacquet.

Liverpool warrant credit for overcoming the stop-start contest Brentford had tried to construct at the start of the second half, striking twice in eight minutes to secure three crucial points and become the first side since Feb. 21, 2026 to beat the Bees on their own patch.
Vitaly Janelt would earn Brentford’s second red card of the match with only minutes remaining, but the real damage had been done by the game’s first dismissal.

Referee John Brooks was in the spotlight. / Julian Finney/Getty ImagesThere was a collective gasp of incredulity which swept around the Gtech when the giant screen flashed up to signal a VAR review for a possible red card was ongoing right at the end of first-half stoppage time. Plenty of the crowd’s whispers were asking which team, let alone which player, was at risk of being dismissed.
As the replays (which weren’t shown to the in-stadium fans) would reveal, Brentford’s Yarmoliuk had been lured into a brainless brush of his head against Jacquet while preparing to defend a corner.

Minutes earlier, VAR had rightly denied Liverpool a penalty, but the fates of Stockley Park rarely side with one team for long. This distant intervention came after a first-half which Brentford had fairly won, limiting their visitors to one big chance which Bradley Barcola fluffed before converting the single clear sight of goal that they created.

The halftime substitutions set the tone for the second 45 minutes. While Keith Andrews reinforced his rearguard before sending on the jet-heeled Kevin Schade to offer a threat in transition, Iraola went all out. Víctor Muñoz, Liverpool’s right winger, replaced Ronald Araújo, a natural center back, in a very loose interpretation of the right back role. Fittingly enough, it would be Muñoz who equalized for the visitors shortly after the hour mark.

Brentford’s bold positioning had pinned Liverpool back in the first half, helping the hosts rack up more shots on target and touches in the opposition penalty area than their illustrious visitors. Yet, with their number reduced, the Bees were either penned inside their own area or left exposed when they dared to venture forward.

Muñoz’s electric speed would exploit this disorganization while Isak benefited from the field being tilted towards Kelleher’s box. The sheer volume of black shirts ensured that Barcola’s header had a decent chance of picking out a teammate. Isak was first onto the scene, taking a deft touch before swiping the ball into the far corner.
After watching their 10 men crumble, Brentford fans could scarcely be blamed for chanting: “To the referee, 2–1.”
Florian Wirtz’s ball control is not the issue. / Liverpool FC/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Alisson—7.0: Deceived by Keane Lewis-Potter’s clever header from range but otherwise not unduly troubled.
RB: Ronald Araújo—6.1: Skirted around the fringes of the contest before he was sacrificed for a far more front-footed approach from the visitors in the second half.

CB: Jérémy Jacquet—7.9: It’s hard to describe the regal Frenchman as anything other than classy; be it the way he strode forward on the ball, clipped passes over befuddled red and white shirts or got his toe to any loose pass. Jacquet even managed to tussle with Igor Thiago without getting his shirt wrinkled.
CB: Virgil van Dijk—8.0: Forced out of his leisurely stroll more often than he would perhaps care but did the grubby part of the game well.

LB: Milos Kerkez—7.7: Seemed to benefit from having his countryman Dominik Szoboszlai in such close proximity to him, constantly adjusting his position while being peppered with instructions. Kerkez looked a little more unsettled after his compatriot’s enforced removal.
CM: Dominik Szoboszlai—6.6: Uncharacteristically disciplined defensively during his brief cameo.
CM: Alexis Mac Allister—8.4: It was his sloppy pass that allowed Brentford to keep Liverpool pinned in before Keane Lewis-Potter nodded in the opener.
